newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips restrucuturing some TV operations.
newsitem.headline: Philips restrucuturing some TV operations.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday that it was restrucuturing television operations in Belgium, France and Italy as part of a previously announced restructuring of its sound and vision unit.
It said jobs at the three sites would fall by 50 percent to around 1,400 as a result of the restructuring in 1997.
The three plants -- at Bruges in Belgium, Dreux in France and Monza in Italy -- are involved in manufacturing and development.

The restructuring changes mean Monza will stop its activities in mid-1997, while Bruges will be the world-wide high-end colour television development centre with a production facility, while Dreux will be the final assembly centre for western Europe.
Dreux will also have a limited development capacity for the regional adaptations of global product platforms.
Philips has already announced a restructuring of plants in Krefeld and Nuremburg in Germany; Dendermonde in Belgium and Vienna in Austria.
Together with today's restructuring some 2,500 jobs are being cut in the division's industrial activities in western Europe.

In marketing and sales, some 850 jobs in 16 European countries have been cut, while 350 research and development jobs are also going. Together with 150 jobs in staff departments the total western European job cuts will be around 3,900.
Philips said the sound and vision restructuring process was on schedule, while further initiatives were being prepared for its operations in the rest of the world.
Philips employs 270,000 people in 60 countries. The consumer products division, which includes sound and vision, employed a total workforce of over 70,000 at end-June.
